chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The ablution before the meal: the owner of the house begins, so that one person is not embarrassed. So when they finish from the meal, he begins with the one on his right, whether he be a freeman or a slave.

He said, 'And in another Hadith: First the lord of the house washes his hand, then he begins with the one on his right. And when the meal is raised, he begins with the one on the left of the owner of the house, and the last one to wash his hand will be the owner of the house, because he is more deserving of patience with the stains.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْبَيْتِ: The owner of the house / host

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for the host regarding ablution and hand washing before and after a meal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the etiquette of handwashing before and after meals, emphasizing the host's role in facilitating comfort for guests. The host washes first to avoid embarrassing guests and last to endure the mess (*ghamar*), reflecting a practical application of humility and service. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on social grace and the spiritual dimension of daily acts like eating.
